cards.text: Right before this, Zion said, 'The LORD has forsaken me; the Lord has forgotten me!' (Isa 49:14). Now the LORD speaks, and He opens with a question: 'Where is your mother’s certificate of divorce with which I sent her away?'
Then question number two: 'Or to which of My creditors did I sell you?' Friend, I got sold for a quarter out of a clearance bin, so trust me, I know what being sold feels like.

cards.question: The LORD tells His people the real reason they were sold and their mother was sent away. What is it?

answers.text: Debts the LORD owed to others

cards.text: Next He asks, 'Why was no one there when I arrived? Why did no one answer when I called?' Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer hoping somebody would call my name, and here the LORD is calling and NOBODY picks up.

cards.question: The LORD asks if His hand is too short to redeem His people. True or false: He says He lacks the strength to deliver them.
Instead, the LORD shows His power. He says He turns rivers into a desert. What does His rebuke do to the sea?

cards.text: And the fish rot for lack of water and die of thirst. Friend, when the FISH are thirsty, you know you're dealing with Somebody, and He's not done yet.

cards.question: The LORD's power reaches past the sea and the rivers. He says He clothes the ___ in black and makes sackcloth their covering.

cards.text: Now a new voice speaks: the LORD's Servant (Isa 50:10). The Servant says, 'The Lord GOD has given Me the tongue of discipleship, to sustain the weary with a word.'

cards.question: Morning by morning, what does the Lord GOD do for the Servant?

answers.text: Sends Him a dream at night
Shows Him a vision of heaven

cards.question: The Lord GOD has opened the Servant's ears. True or false: the Servant says He turned back.

cards.text: Then it gets hard. The Servant says, 'I offered My back to those who struck Me, and My cheeks to those who tore out My beard.'

cards.question: True or false: when people scorn the Servant and spit on Him, He hides His face.
Because the Lord GOD helps Him, the Servant says He has set His face like ___.

cards.text: The Servant also says He has not been disgraced, and 'I know that I will not be put to shame.' Friend, I can't even be sure my cookies are done, and I've got a TIMER.

cards.question: Then the Servant asks, 'Who will dare to contend with Me?' Why is He so bold?

answers.text: The One who vindicates Him is near
His enemies have all run away
An army stands right behind Him

cards.text: Then He says, 'Who has a case against Me? Let him approach Me!' Meanwhile, somebody leaves ONE bad review about my sprinkles and I'm hiding behind the oven for a WEEK.

cards.question: The Lord GOD helps the Servant, so who can condemn Him? He says they will all wear out like a ___, and the moths will devour them.

cards.text: Then a question goes out to everyone listening: 'Who among you fears the LORD and obeys the voice of His Servant? Who among you walks in darkness and has no light?'

cards.question: After the questions about fearing the LORD and walking in darkness, a word comes: 'Let him…' Let him do what?

answers.text: Trust in the name of the LORD

cards.text: Then one more line: 'let him lean on his God.' Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer, and I did NOT get out of there by leaning on myself.
Then the passage speaks to another group: 'Behold, all you who kindle a fire, who array yourselves with firebrands, walk in the light of your fire and of the firebrands you have lit!'

cards.question: Some walk by the light of fires they lit themselves. They're told, 'This is what you will receive from My hand.' What is it?

findings.problem: The opening card says who is speaking (the LORD) and gives context, but never says to whom. The LORD addresses the people whose 'mother' was sent away, but the card leaves that out. 'His people' first appears on card 3.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: 'Right before this, Zion said...' is not accurate. Isaiah 49:14 is not right before 50:1. The LORD's long reply in Isaiah 49:15-26 comes between them. Something like 'Earlier, Zion said...' would be true.

rule.text: Noticing: What he points out must be true.

findings.problem: The question asks 'Why is He so bold?' and makes 'The One who vindicates Him is near' the reason for the challenge 'Who will dare to contend with Me?' Isaiah 50:8 places the two lines side by side but does not state a cause. (Verse 7 uses 'therefore', but verse 8 does not.) The question adds a reason, and it also closes a connection the text leaves open.

rule.text: Reasons: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: The question includes 'and the moths will devour them', which rules out the wrong answers 'candle' and 'field', because moths eat garments. The clue turns the card into a giveaway instead of a reasoned pick. The moth clause could be dropped from the question, or the wrong answers replaced with things moths could plausibly eat.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: All three true-or-false cards in the walkthrough (stop 1 card 5, stop 2 card 3, stop 2 card 5) have False as the right answer. Each one is built the same way: it negates what the speaker says. A baker can learn to pick False without reasoning. The 'No formula' rule covers question types, their order and where blanks fall, but not the balance of true and false answers.
findings.question: Should true-or-false cards across a walkthrough (or a stop) be required to mix True and False right answers, and avoid always negating the text?
